facts.fact: INSEED reports that in April 2026 a national workshop in Lome trained about thirty statistical-system staff to migrate datasets from Togo's existing Open Data Portal 1.0 to ODP 2.0, the national open data platform for INSEED and sector ministries; no dataset count or licence is stated.

facts.fact: Togo First, 18 November 2025, recalls that in December 2024 Togo launched two public data dissemination platforms, Open Data and the Geoportail Open Data, run by the Agence Togo Digital; it does not tie them to an open data policy.

facts.fact: La Voix de la Nation reports that the Open Data portal (opendata.gouv.tg) and the Geoportail (geodata.gouv.tg) were officially launched in December 2024 by the digital ministry through its operational arm, the Agence Togo Digital; the article names no open data policy.

The article states the Geoportail centralises data from 23 ministries and more than 550 administrative units, drawn from a 2021-2022 collection under the PRISE project; the article is dated 2025-01-08 and gives no date for the figure, so that date is used.

facts.fact: The terms of use of opendata.gouv.tg, run by Agence Togo Digital, say data published on the platform is accessible under an open licence unless indicated otherwise, without naming a specific licence.

CIOMAG reports the Ministry of Digital Economy launched the geoportail.gouv.tg government geoportal on 6 May 2025 with an open-data version, geodata.gouv.tg, for the public, researchers and investors; no open licence is mentioned.

The Ministry of Digital Economy launched the national Geoportail on 6 May 2025, with an open public tier at geodata.gouv.tg of over 800 map layers across 15 sectors that users can view, analyse and download.
